lines: +pnpr now keeps hosted package metadata in SQLite by default, at `<storage>/.metadata/metadata.sqlite`. The `metadata` block names the database by URL, such as `url: sqlite:./metadata.sqlite`. The `metadata` block no longer accepts `backend: sqlite` or `path`. A registry with an `s3:` block and no metadata URL keeps package documents in the bucket. pnpr does not import the package documents of an existing filesystem store. Republish its packages after upgrading.

-pnpr can keep hosted package metadata in an embedded SQLite database with `metadata: { backend: sqlite }`. With SQLite metadata, pnpr refuses any change to a published npm version's manifest. pnpr never accepts an unpublished version again, even when its tombstone is lost. pnpr records who moved each dist-tag, and when. Hosted npm package responses carry a `pnpr-generation` header.
